questions.prompt: Which option runs EC2 instances on hardware dedicated to a single customer, without giving visibility or control over sockets and cores?
questions.explanation: Dedicated Instances provide single-tenant hardware; Dedicated Hosts add host-level visibility needed for server-bound licenses.

questions.prompt: How are On-Demand Linux EC2 instances billed?
choices: Per day, with a 24-hour minimum charge
questions.explanation: Linux On-Demand instances use per-second billing with a one-minute minimum.

questions.prompt: A startup plans to run its entire backend on AWS Lambda. What will determine its Lambda compute cost?
choices: A flat monthly fee charged for each function that is deployed
The number of requests and the duration of execution based on memory allocated
The number of servers provisioned in advance to run the functions
The size of the deployment package only, regardless of invocations
questions.explanation: Lambda charges for requests and compute duration in GB-seconds; there are no servers to pay for.

questions.prompt: Which factors primarily determine Amazon S3 charges?
choices: Storage used and class, number of requests, and data transferred out
The number of buckets created and the IAM users who can access them
The number of Availability Zones available in the chosen Region
The number of objects encrypted with S3 managed keys each month
questions.explanation: S3 pricing is based on storage amount and class, requests and retrievals, and data transfer out.

questions.prompt: A company wants AWS to automatically apply a restrictive IAM policy when its monthly spend exceeds a threshold. Which feature should it use?
questions.explanation: Budgets actions can apply IAM or SCP policies or stop instances when a budget threshold is crossed.

questions.prompt: Where can a company view Savings Plans and Reserved Instance purchase recommendations based on its past usage?
questions.explanation: Cost Explorer analyzes historical usage to recommend Savings Plans and RIs; the Pricing Calculator only estimates planned costs.

questions.prompt: A developer wants to ask questions and get answers from the AWS community and AWS experts. Which resource should they use?
questions.explanation: AWS re:Post is the community-driven question-and-answer service for AWS topics.

questions.prompt: Which resource contains articles and videos that answer the questions AWS Support receives most often?
questions.explanation: The Knowledge Center, part of re:Post, covers the most frequent questions and requests that AWS Support receives.

questions.prompt: Which AWS resource offers time-tested strategies, guides and patterns from AWS experts to accelerate migration and modernization projects?
questions.explanation: AWS Prescriptive Guidance provides vetted strategies, guides and patterns for migration and modernization.

questions.prompt: A large enterprise wants a global team of AWS experts to help it achieve specific business outcomes during a major cloud transformation. Which offering fits?
questions.explanation: AWS Professional Services is a team of experts that works with customers on cloud adoption and transformation projects.

questions.prompt: Which AWS Trusted Advisor category warns you when your usage approaches a service quota?
questions.explanation: The service limits (quotas) category flags usage above 80% of a quota.

questions.prompt: Which service lets you view your quotas for AWS services and request quota increases from one place?
questions.explanation: Service Quotas centrally shows applied quota values and lets you request increases.

questions.prompt: With consolidated billing in AWS Organizations, how are Reserved Instance discounts handled across member accounts?
choices: They expire as soon as a different member account uses them
They apply only to the account that purchased them, without exception
They are converted into Spot pricing for the other member accounts
They can be shared across accounts in the organization by default
questions.explanation: RI and Savings Plans discount sharing is enabled by default across accounts in a consolidated billing family.

questions.prompt: A company's Amazon S3 bill shows a lower price per GB once its stored data passes certain amounts. What is this pricing approach called?
questions.explanation: Tiered pricing means you pay less per unit as your usage grows.

questions.prompt: Which AWS service has no additional charge, so you pay only for the AWS resources it provisions?
questions.explanation: CloudFormation is free for AWS resource types; you pay for the resources it creates.

questions.prompt: Which commitment terms are available for EC2 Reserved Instances and Savings Plans?
questions.explanation: Both RIs and Savings Plans are offered with 1-year or 3-year terms.

questions.prompt: A company no longer needs some of its Standard Reserved Instances. Where can it sell the remaining term to other AWS customers?
questions.explanation: Eligible Standard RIs can be listed and sold on the Reserved Instance Marketplace.

questions.prompt: Which feature consolidates cost optimization recommendations, such as rightsizing and idle resources, across accounts and Regions in one place?
questions.explanation: Cost Optimization Hub aggregates and prioritizes savings recommendations across an organization.

questions.prompt: A team moves its containers from self-managed EC2 instances to AWS Fargate. What will determine its compute cost?
choices: A fixed fee charged for each container image stored in the registry
The number of EC2 instances that are registered in the cluster
The vCPU and memory resources requested for the tasks over time
The number of Availability Zones the service is deployed across
questions.explanation: Fargate charges for vCPU, memory and storage requested by tasks, with no EC2 instances to manage.

questions.prompt: Which AWS program provides eligible startups with credits, technical support and training?
questions.explanation: AWS Activate offers startups AWS credits, support and resources.

questions.prompt: A team wants a CloudWatch alarm that notifies them when estimated AWS charges exceed $500. Which CloudWatch billing metric should the alarm use?
questions.explanation: Billing alarms use the EstimatedCharges metric, published in the US East (N. Virginia) Region.

questions.prompt: When using Amazon S3, which security task is the customer's responsibility?
choices: Replacing failed disks in the S3 fleet
Configuring bucket policies and access permissions
Patching the storage servers that host S3
Maintaining the physical security of S3 facilities
questions.explanation: AWS secures the S3 infrastructure; customers control who can access their buckets and objects.

questions.prompt: For a fully managed service such as Amazon DynamoDB, which task is handled by AWS?
choices: Patching the underlying operating systems and infrastructure
Classifying the sensitivity of the stored data
Deciding which IAM users can read and write each table
Writing the application logic that queries tables
questions.explanation: With managed services AWS patches the infrastructure, while customers manage access and data.

questions.prompt: Which component is AWS's responsibility when a customer runs Amazon EC2 instances?
choices: The application installed on the instance
questions.explanation: AWS secures the host and virtualization infrastructure; the guest OS and above belong to the customer for EC2.

questions.prompt: Controls such as physical and environmental protections that a customer fully inherits from AWS are called what?
questions.explanation: Inherited controls are fully provided by AWS; shared controls like patch management apply to both parties in their own contexts.

questions.prompt: As a customer moves a workload from Amazon EC2 to AWS Lambda, how does its share of security responsibility change?
choices: It stays exactly the same at every layer of the technology stack
It increases, because the customer must now patch the Lambda host servers
It shifts entirely to AWS, including the customer's own data and access rights
It decreases, because AWS manages more of the stack such as the OS and runtime
questions.explanation: Higher-level services shift OS and platform responsibilities to AWS, but customers still own code, data and permissions.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between authentication and authorization in AWS IAM?
choices: Both terms describe verifying a password at the sign-in page
Authentication verifies who you are; authorization determines what you can do
Authentication grants permissions, while authorization verifies a user's identity
Authorization applies only to actions taken by the root user
questions.explanation: Signing in with credentials is authentication; policies then authorize or deny specific actions.

questions.prompt: What are IAM access keys primarily used for?
choices: Signing in to the AWS Management Console with a username
Connecting to Linux EC2 instances over an SSH session
Programmatic access to AWS through the CLI, SDKs or APIs
Encrypting objects stored in Amazon S3 buckets at rest
questions.explanation: An access key ID and secret access key sign programmatic requests; console sign-in uses a password.

questions.prompt: A policy attached to an IAM user, group or role that defines what that identity can do is called what?
questions.explanation: Identity-based policies attach to identities; resource-based policies attach to resources such as S3 buckets.

questions.prompt: Which type of IAM policy is created and maintained by AWS for common job functions and use cases?
questions.explanation: AWS managed policies are maintained by AWS; customer managed and inline policies are written by the customer.

questions.prompt: An external auditor working in a different AWS account needs temporary read-only access to your account. What is the MOST secure approach?
choices: Make the relevant S3 buckets public until the audit is complete
Share the root user password with the auditor for the audit period
Create an IAM role with read-only permissions that the auditor's account can assume
Create an IAM user for the auditor and email its long-term access keys
questions.explanation: Cross-account roles provide temporary credentials without sharing long-term secrets.

questions.prompt: In AWS IAM Identity Center, what defines the level of access that users and groups receive in an AWS account?
questions.explanation: Permission sets are collections of policies that Identity Center provisions as roles in target accounts.

questions.prompt: Employees should sign in to the AWS console using their existing corporate Active Directory credentials instead of new IAM users. Which approach is BEST?
choices: Share a single administrator IAM user among all of the employees
Connect IAM Identity Center to the corporate directory for federated access
Create an IAM user for every employee using the same initial password
Give each employee their own set of root user access keys
questions.explanation: Federation lets users reuse existing corporate identities and receive temporary AWS credentials.

questions.prompt: Which service provides a managed Microsoft Active Directory in the AWS Cloud?
questions.explanation: AWS Directory Service offers AWS Managed Microsoft AD and AD Connector.

questions.prompt: Which IAM feature shows when a user or role last used each AWS service, helping you remove unused permissions?
questions.explanation: Last accessed data shows service usage by an identity; the credential report focuses on credential status.

questions.prompt: Which tool lets you test IAM policies to see whether specific actions would be allowed or denied before applying them?
questions.explanation: The IAM policy simulator evaluates policies against chosen actions and resources for troubleshooting.

questions.prompt: An administrator creates a new IAM user for a contractor and attaches no policies. What permissions does the user have?
choices: The same permissions as the account root user
No permissions until a policy grants them
questions.explanation: IAM denies everything implicitly; permissions must be explicitly granted by policies.

questions.prompt: Which IAM feature sets the maximum permissions that identity-based policies can grant to a specific user or role?
questions.explanation: A permissions boundary limits a single IAM entity; SCPs limit accounts in AWS Organizations.

questions.prompt: A team needs to store application configuration values and a few encrypted strings at low cost and does not need automatic rotation. Which service is MOST suitable?
questions.explanation: Parameter Store holds encrypted parameters; Secrets Manager adds native automatic rotation.

questions.prompt: A company wants the data on its EC2 instance's EBS volumes protected even if the underlying storage is accessed. Enabling EBS encryption protects data in which state?
questions.explanation: EBS encryption protects data stored on the volume and its snapshots; TLS protects data in transit.

questions.prompt: Which type of AWS KMS key gives the customer full control over its key policy, rotation settings and the ability to disable it?
questions.explanation: Customer managed keys are created and controlled by the customer; AWS managed keys are controlled by AWS on the customer's behalf.

questions.prompt: A company must encrypt files before uploading them to Amazon S3 so AWS never handles plaintext data. Which approach meets this requirement?
choices: Server-side encryption with S3 managed keys
questions.explanation: With client-side encryption the data is encrypted before it leaves the customer's environment.

questions.prompt: A website receives floods of HTTP requests from a few IP addresses. Which AWS WAF feature can automatically block IPs that exceed a request threshold?
questions.explanation: Rate-based rules count requests per IP and block those that exceed the limit.

questions.prompt: Which AWS CloudTrail feature lets you store events and run SQL-based queries on them for investigations?
questions.explanation: CloudTrail Lake is a managed data lake for activity events that supports SQL queries.

questions.prompt: How can a company prove that its CloudTrail log files were not modified or deleted after delivery?
choices: Enable CloudTrail log file integrity validation
Turn on Amazon GuardDuty for the whole account
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the log bucket
Also send the log data to VPC Flow Logs
questions.explanation: Integrity validation uses digest files with hashing and signing to detect changes to log files.

questions.prompt: Which service checks an account for issues such as security groups allowing unrestricted access to specific ports and exposed access keys?
questions.explanation: Trusted Advisor's security checks flag risks like open ports, missing root MFA and exposed access keys.

questions.prompt: A company must ensure its customer data is stored only in Germany. Which approach BEST supports this requirement?
choices: Store the data in a CloudFront edge location located in Germany
Use whatever default Region AWS selects for each service automatically
Deploy only in the Frankfurt Region and use an SCP to deny other Regions
Deploy in any Region and rely on CloudFront caching to keep the data local
questions.explanation: AWS does not move data out of a Region without customer action, and an SCP can prevent use of other Regions.

questions.prompt: Which statement about service control policies (SCPs) is accurate?
choices: They replace the need for any IAM policies in member accounts
They limit the maximum permissions in member accounts but do not grant permissions
They apply only to the root user of the management account
They grant full administrator access to every member account automatically
questions.explanation: SCPs act as guardrails; IAM policies are still required to grant permissions.

questions.prompt: Which statement about SCPs and the AWS Organizations management account is correct?
choices: SCPs apply most strictly to the management account
SCPs do not restrict users or roles in the management account
The management account cannot attach SCPs
SCPs automatically delete unused IAM users in the management account
questions.explanation: SCPs affect member accounts only, which is one reason to avoid running workloads in the management account.

questions.prompt: In AWS Control Tower, a control that uses SCPs to disallow certain actions is which type of control?
questions.explanation: Preventive controls block actions using SCPs; detective controls use AWS Config rules to find noncompliance.

questions.prompt: Which AWS Config feature packages a collection of Config rules and remediation actions that can be deployed as a single entity?
questions.explanation: Conformance packs bundle rules and remediations for compliance frameworks across accounts and Regions.

questions.prompt: Administrators want users to deploy only approved, preconfigured products such as CloudFormation templates. Which service supports this governance requirement?
questions.explanation: Service Catalog lets organizations create and govern catalogs of approved IT products.

questions.prompt: Which AWS Organizations policy type helps standardize tags applied to resources across accounts?
questions.explanation: Tag policies define rules for tag keys and values to keep tagging consistent.

questions.prompt: Which service securely shares resources such as subnets and Transit Gateways with other accounts in an organization?
questions.explanation: AWS RAM shares supported resources across accounts without duplicating them.

questions.prompt: What are the default rules of a newly created custom security group?
choices: All inbound traffic is denied and all outbound traffic is allowed
All traffic is denied in both directions permanently
All inbound traffic is allowed and all outbound traffic is denied
All inbound and outbound traffic is allowed
questions.explanation: New security groups have no inbound rules and an allow-all outbound rule.

questions.prompt: Can a security group contain explicit deny rules?
choices: Yes, and deny rules are always evaluated first
Yes, but only for outbound traffic
Only when attached to a load balancer
No, security groups support allow rules only
questions.explanation: Security groups only allow traffic; use network ACLs to explicitly deny traffic.

questions.prompt: Administrators need secure shell access to EC2 instances without opening inbound SSH ports or managing SSH keys. Which feature should they use?
questions.explanation: Session Manager provides audited, browser or CLI shell access without inbound ports or bastion hosts.

questions.prompt: Which service lets a company create its own private certificate authority to issue certificates for internal applications?
questions.explanation: AWS Private CA issues private certificates; ACM public certificates are for internet-facing endpoints.

questions.prompt: A compliance officer asks whether a new DynamoDB table must be specially configured to encrypt data at rest. Which statement is correct?
choices: It requires an AWS CloudHSM cluster
It is enabled by default for all tables
It must be purchased as a separate add-on
It is available only for global tables
questions.explanation: DynamoDB encrypts all table data at rest by default using KMS keys.

questions.prompt: A user without AWS credentials needs to download one private S3 object for the next hour. What is the MOST secure solution?
choices: Make the bucket public for one hour only
Share an IAM user's long-term access keys
Generate a presigned URL that expires in one hour
Disable S3 Block Public Access temporarily for the account
questions.explanation: Presigned URLs grant time-limited access to a specific object without changing bucket permissions.

questions.prompt: Which S3 feature requires multi-factor authentication to permanently delete an object version or change the bucket's versioning state?
questions.explanation: MFA Delete adds an MFA requirement for permanent version deletion and versioning changes.

questions.prompt: What is the recommended practice for long-term IAM access keys?
choices: Embed them in application source code so deployments are simpler
Rotate them regularly and prefer temporary credentials from roles where possible
Share them across teams to keep the total number of keys small
Never rotate them, to avoid breaking applications that depend on them
questions.explanation: Long-term keys should be minimized, protected and rotated; roles provide automatically rotated temporary credentials.

questions.prompt: Which service issues temporary, limited-privilege security credentials when a role is assumed?
questions.explanation: AWS STS issues the temporary credentials used when assuming IAM roles and for federation.

questions.prompt: Using AWS WAF, security groups, network ACLs and encryption together to protect one application is an example of which concept?
questions.explanation: Defense in depth applies multiple layers of security controls so one failure does not expose the system.

questions.prompt: A company wants to be notified whenever the root user signs in to the console. Which combination is MOST appropriate?
choices: Use AWS Cost Explorer to look for any charges caused by the root user each month
Enable S3 Versioning on the bucket where the account's logs are stored
Create an AWS Budgets alert that triggers whenever someone signs in
Match the CloudTrail ConsoleLogin event with an EventBridge rule that notifies SNS
questions.explanation: CloudTrail records ConsoleLogin events, and EventBridge can match them and send an SNS notification.

questions.prompt: Which resource can AWS WAF be associated with to inspect web requests?
choices: An Amazon API Gateway REST API
questions.explanation: AWS WAF protects resources such as CloudFront, Application Load Balancers, API Gateway and AppSync.

questions.prompt: How can a company capture API activity from every account in its AWS organization in one trail?
choices: Create an organization trail in AWS CloudTrail from the management account
Turn on Amazon Macie in the management account for all Regions
Create VPC peering connections between all of the member accounts
Enable AWS Budgets in each member account and export reports
questions.explanation: An organization trail logs events for all member accounts to a central location.

questions.prompt: Which AWS Config feature collects configuration and compliance data from multiple accounts and Regions into a single account?
questions.explanation: A Config aggregator gives a centralized multi-account, multi-Region view.

questions.prompt: A customer is concerned about its data on failed disks in AWS facilities. Who is responsible for securely destroying failed storage devices in AWS data centers?
choices: The customer whose data was stored
The customer and AWS jointly on site
An AWS Partner chosen by the customer
questions.explanation: Media decommissioning is part of security of the cloud, which AWS performs using industry-standard sanitization.

questions.prompt: A company wants users to access files in an S3 bucket only through its CloudFront distribution, not directly from S3. What should it configure?
choices: A NAT gateway placed in a public subnet
questions.explanation: Origin access control lets only the CloudFront distribution read the bucket, blocking direct access.

questions.prompt: Can one IAM group be added as a member of another IAM group?
choices: Yes, up to five levels deep
No, IAM groups cannot be nested
Yes, but only for administrator groups
questions.explanation: IAM groups contain users only; they cannot contain other groups.

questions.prompt: Which feature can generate a least-privilege IAM policy based on the actions an identity actually performed in CloudTrail?
questions.explanation: Access Analyzer can review CloudTrail activity and generate a policy containing only the used permissions.

questions.prompt: A US government contractor must run workloads that meet FedRAMP High and ITAR requirements. Which AWS option is designed for this?
questions.explanation: GovCloud (US) Regions are isolated Regions designed for sensitive and regulated US government workloads.

questions.prompt: Which is a supported MFA option for IAM users and the root user?
choices: A one-time link sent by email
A FIDO2 security key or passkey
questions.explanation: AWS supports passkeys and FIDO security keys, virtual authenticator apps and hardware TOTP tokens.

questions.prompt: What additional capability does server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) provide compared with SSE-S3?
choices: Encryption of data in transit between clients and the Amazon S3 endpoint
Free storage for any objects that are encrypted at rest
Control over key policies and an audit trail of key usage in CloudTrail
Automatic deletion of encrypted objects after a retention period
questions.explanation: SSE-KMS lets you manage key permissions and see key usage logged in CloudTrail; SSE-S3 keys are fully managed by S3.

questions.prompt: How long does CloudTrail event history keep management events at no additional charge?
questions.explanation: Event history shows the past 90 days of management events; create a trail or use CloudTrail Lake to retain longer.

questions.prompt: A security team needs to see what a specific security group's rules looked like last week and how they changed. Which service provides this?
questions.explanation: AWS Config keeps a configuration history timeline for resources; CloudTrail records who made the API calls.

questions.prompt: An S3 bucket is found without encryption by an AWS Config rule. How can the issue be fixed automatically?
choices: Create a new IAM group and add the bucket owner as a member
Enable AWS Budgets alerts that notify the owner of the bucket
Attach a remediation action that runs a Systems Manager Automation document
Turn on Amazon CloudFront in front of the bucket to encrypt it
questions.explanation: Config rules support automatic remediation through Systems Manager Automation runbooks.

questions.prompt: Which statement about AWS KMS keys is correct?
choices: Keys are shared automatically with all AWS accounts
Keys can be downloaded in plaintext for backup
Key material never leaves KMS unencrypted
Keys are stored in the customer's S3 bucket
questions.explanation: KMS keys are protected by FIPS-validated hardware security modules and are used only inside the service.

questions.prompt: A company wants one member account to manage Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub for the entire organization. Which feature enables this?
choices: Assigning a permissions boundary to the root user
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations lets you designate a delegated administrator for supported security services.

questions.prompt: A team has an unencrypted Amazon RDS DB instance and needs an encrypted copy. What should it do?
choices: Move the DB instance into a private subnet in another Availability Zone
Enable encryption directly on the running DB instance from the console
Take a snapshot, copy it with encryption enabled, and restore from the copy
Attach an AWS WAF web ACL to the DB instance to encrypt its traffic
questions.explanation: Encryption cannot be turned on for an existing RDS instance; an encrypted snapshot copy can be restored instead.

questions.prompt: A developer wants to call AWS services directly from a Python application. Which tool should they use?
choices: An AWS SDK, such as Boto3 for Python
questions.explanation: AWS SDKs provide language-specific APIs for calling AWS services from application code.

questions.prompt: Which tool provides a browser-based shell that is pre-authenticated with your console credentials and includes the AWS CLI?
questions.explanation: CloudShell opens from the console with the AWS CLI preinstalled and your credentials already available.

questions.prompt: An administrator wants to automate repetitive AWS tasks with shell scripts run from a terminal. Which tool is MOST suitable?
questions.explanation: The AWS CLI lets you control AWS services from the command line and script them.

questions.prompt: Which EC2 instance family offers a balance of compute, memory and networking for workloads such as web servers and code repositories?
questions.explanation: General purpose instances like M and T families balance resources for diverse workloads.

questions.prompt: A data warehousing application needs high sequential read and write access to very large datasets on local storage. Which EC2 instance family fits best?
questions.explanation: Storage optimized instances deliver high IOPS and throughput from local storage.

questions.prompt: A team wants every new EC2 instance to launch with the same hardened operating system and preinstalled software. What should they create and launch from?
questions.explanation: An AMI provides the template, including OS and software, from which instances launch.

questions.prompt: A team wants a script to install software automatically when an EC2 instance first boots. Which feature should they use?
questions.explanation: User data scripts run at launch to bootstrap an instance.

questions.prompt: In an EC2 Auto Scaling group, which setting defines the smallest number of instances the group will keep running?
questions.explanation: Minimum capacity is the floor; desired is the current target and maximum is the ceiling.

questions.prompt: An application must process each image as soon as it is uploaded to Amazon S3, without managing servers. What is the BEST solution?
choices: Trigger an AWS Lambda function from an S3 event notification
Use Amazon Lightsail to watch the bucket
Run a cron job on an EC2 instance that polls the bucket every minute
Use AWS Snowball to copy the images
questions.explanation: S3 event notifications can invoke Lambda directly, giving serverless event-driven processing.

questions.prompt: A developer wants to deploy a Java web application while AWS handles provisioning, load balancing, scaling and health monitoring, and still be able to access the underlying resources. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Elastic Beanstalk automates deployment and scaling while leaving the EC2 and other resources accessible.

questions.prompt: Which S3 storage class is designed for data accessed infrequently but requiring millisecond access, stored across multiple Availability Zones?
questions.explanation: Standard-IA offers lower storage cost with multi-AZ resilience and millisecond retrieval, plus a retrieval fee.

questions.prompt: A hospital keeps medical images that are accessed about once a quarter but must be retrieved in milliseconds. Which S3 storage class is MOST cost-effective?
questions.explanation: Glacier Instant Retrieval is the lowest-cost storage for rarely accessed data that still needs millisecond access.

questions.prompt: Which S3 storage class suits archive data with retrieval times from minutes to hours and free bulk retrievals?
questions.explanation: Glacier Flexible Retrieval offers expedited, standard and free bulk retrieval options for archives.

questions.prompt: A company must automatically copy new objects from an S3 bucket in us-east-1 to a bucket in eu-west-1 for disaster recovery. Which feature should it use?
questions.explanation: Cross-Region Replication asynchronously copies objects to a bucket in another Region.

questions.prompt: Users far from a bucket's Region upload large files slowly. Which feature speeds up long-distance uploads by routing through CloudFront edge locations?
questions.explanation: Transfer Acceleration uses the AWS edge network to optimize transfers to S3 over long distances.

questions.prompt: A company wants to host a simple static marketing website made of HTML, CSS and images without managing servers. Which option is simplest?
choices: Amazon EC2 with an Apache web server
questions.explanation: S3 can serve static websites directly, often combined with CloudFront.

questions.prompt: How are Amazon EBS snapshots stored?
choices: On the customer's on-premises storage through Storage Gateway
Only within the same Availability Zone as the source volume
As full copies stored on the instance store of the attached instance
Incrementally, saving only changed blocks, in AWS-managed S3 storage
questions.explanation: EBS snapshots are incremental and stored durably in S3, managed by AWS.

questions.prompt: A mission-critical database requires sustained high IOPS with low latency on block storage. Which EBS volume type is MOST appropriate?
questions.explanation: Provisioned IOPS SSD volumes are designed for I/O-intensive databases needing consistent performance.

questions.prompt: Which service continuously replicates on-premises or cloud servers to AWS so they can be recovered quickly after an outage?
questions.explanation: Elastic Disaster Recovery provides fast, low-cost recovery using continuous block-level replication.

questions.prompt: Which database engine is available on Amazon RDS?
questions.explanation: RDS supports Aurora, MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server and Db2; the others are non-relational.

questions.prompt: A mobile game needs a serverless database for its leaderboard with consistent single-digit millisecond performance at any scale. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: DynamoDB is a serverless key-value database delivering single-digit millisecond performance at scale.

questions.prompt: Which DynamoDB feature provides a fully managed, multi-Region, multi-active database for globally distributed applications?
questions.explanation: Global tables replicate data across Regions and allow reads and writes in each Region.

questions.prompt: An application with intermittent, unpredictable traffic needs a relational database that automatically adjusts capacity. Which option fits?
choices: Amazon RDS on a fixed instance size
questions.explanation: Aurora Serverless v2 scales database capacity automatically based on demand.

questions.prompt: A company runs Apache Cassandra workloads and wants a managed, serverless, compatible service. Which should it choose?
questions.explanation: Amazon Keyspaces is a managed Cassandra-compatible database; DocumentDB is MongoDB-compatible.

questions.prompt: Which service is a durable, Redis OSS-compatible in-memory database that can serve as a primary database?
questions.explanation: MemoryDB stores data durably with a multi-AZ transaction log, unlike a pure cache.

questions.prompt: When would a company choose to run a database on Amazon EC2 instead of Amazon RDS?
choices: When it needs automatic Multi-AZ failover that AWS fully manages
When it wants the least administrative effort possible for running the database
When it needs operating system access or an engine or configuration RDS does not support
When it wants AWS to handle all database patching and backups
questions.explanation: Self-managing on EC2 gives full control at the cost of more operational work.

questions.prompt: What is an Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC)?
choices: A content delivery network that caches static files at edge locations worldwide
A managed VPN service that remote employees use to reach the office
A logically isolated virtual network in the AWS Cloud that you define and control
A dedicated physical data center that AWS rents to a single customer
questions.explanation: A VPC is your own isolated virtual network with configurable IP ranges, subnets and route tables.

questions.prompt: An architect is designing a highly available VPC across several Availability Zones. Which statement about subnets is correct?
choices: Each subnet resides entirely within one Availability Zone
Each subnet spans all Availability Zones in its Region
Subnets exist only at edge locations
A subnet can span multiple Regions
questions.explanation: Subnets map to a single AZ, so highly available designs use subnets in multiple AZs.

questions.prompt: Two VPCs need to communicate privately using private IP addresses with a simple one-to-one connection. Which option fits?
questions.explanation: VPC peering connects two VPCs privately; it is not transitive, unlike a Transit Gateway hub.

questions.prompt: Which Route 53 routing policy sends traffic to a secondary site only when health checks show the primary is unhealthy?
questions.explanation: Failover routing supports active-passive configurations using health checks.

questions.prompt: A team wants to send 10% of users to a new application version and 90% to the current one. Which Route 53 routing policy should it use?
questions.explanation: Weighted routing splits traffic across resources in proportions you specify.

questions.prompt: A company must show country-specific content based on where users' DNS queries originate. Which Route 53 routing policy fits?
questions.explanation: Geolocation routing chooses responses based on the user's location, such as country or continent.

questions.prompt: A SaaS provider wants to expose its service privately to customers' VPCs without VPC peering or traversing the internet. Which technology should it use?
questions.explanation: PrivateLink exposes services through interface VPC endpoints using private connectivity.

questions.prompt: Remote employees need to connect securely from their laptops to resources in a VPC. Which managed service fits?
questions.explanation: Client VPN is a managed, client-based VPN for individual users; Site-to-Site VPN connects networks.

questions.prompt: An application needs a static public IPv4 address that can be quickly moved to a standby EC2 instance during a failure. Which feature fits?
questions.explanation: An Elastic IP address is a static public IPv4 address you can associate with different instances.

questions.prompt: A company wants to automatically detect objects, faces and inappropriate content in images uploaded by users. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Rekognition analyzes images and videos; Comprehend analyzes text.

questions.prompt: A retailer wants to determine whether customer product reviews are positive or negative. Which service is designed for this?
questions.explanation: Comprehend uses natural language processing to find sentiment, entities and key phrases in text.

questions.prompt: A call center wants to convert recorded customer calls into text. Which service should it use?
questions.explanation: Transcribe converts speech to text; Polly does the reverse.

questions.prompt: Which service translates text between languages in real time using neural machine translation?
questions.explanation: Amazon Translate provides neural machine translation between languages.

questions.prompt: A company wants to build a conversational chatbot that understands voice and text input. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Lex provides automatic speech recognition and natural language understanding for chatbots.

questions.prompt: Which generative AI assistant helps developers write, explain and transform code in their IDE?
questions.explanation: Amazon Q Developer is AWS's AI assistant for software development tasks.

questions.prompt: Employees need an intelligent search service that finds answers across internal documents using natural language questions. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Kendra is an ML-powered enterprise search service; Athena queries structured data with SQL.

questions.prompt: An online store wants to add real-time personalized product recommendations without ML expertise. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Personalize builds recommendation models using the same technology as Amazon.com.

questions.prompt: Which service helps build a secure data lake on Amazon S3 with centralized, fine-grained access permissions?
questions.explanation: Lake Formation simplifies building data lakes and managing permissions to databases, tables and columns.

questions.prompt: A company runs Apache Kafka for streaming and wants AWS to manage the clusters. Which service fits?
choices: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka
questions.explanation: Amazon MSK is a fully managed Apache Kafka service; Amazon MQ manages ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ.

questions.prompt: An order-processing system must process messages exactly once and in the order they were sent. Which option should it use?
choices: An Amazon SNS standard topic with email
questions.explanation: FIFO queues preserve order and provide exactly-once processing; standard queues offer at-least-once delivery.

questions.prompt: Which service sends transactional and marketing emails, such as order confirmations, at scale?
questions.explanation: Amazon SES is a cloud email service for sending and receiving email.

questions.prompt: A company is migrating an application that uses Apache ActiveMQ and wants a managed broker without rewriting messaging code. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Amazon MQ supports industry-standard protocols for ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ, easing migration.

questions.prompt: Which service securely connects billions of IoT devices to the AWS Cloud and routes their messages?
questions.explanation: IoT Core is the managed cloud service for device connectivity and messaging.

questions.prompt: Factory devices must run local processing and machine learning inference even when disconnected from the internet. Which service provides this edge runtime?
questions.explanation: Greengrass runs local compute, messaging and ML on edge devices with cloud management.

questions.prompt: Which service automates the build, test and deploy stages of a release process as a continuous delivery pipeline?
questions.explanation: CodePipeline orchestrates release stages; CodeBuild and CodeDeploy perform individual stages.

questions.prompt: A team wants to compile source code and run unit tests on every commit without managing build servers. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: CodeBuild is a managed build service that scales automatically.

questions.prompt: A company wants to automate rolling deployments of new application versions to its EC2 fleet and on-premises servers. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: CodeDeploy handles the deployment step, including rolling and blue/green deployments.

questions.prompt: A front-end developer wants to quickly build, host and add authentication to a full-stack web or mobile app. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Amplify provides tools and hosting for building full-stack web and mobile applications.

questions.prompt: Which service provides managed GraphQL APIs that let applications query multiple data sources in a single request?
choices: Amazon API Gateway WebSocket APIs only
questions.explanation: AppSync is a managed GraphQL and Pub/Sub API service.

questions.prompt: A company wants to set up a cloud-based customer contact center with omnichannel support. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Amazon Connect is a cloud contact center service; Lex can be added for chatbots.

questions.prompt: A company wants to give remote employees secure, managed virtual desktops in the cloud. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: WorkSpaces provides persistent virtual desktops; AppStream 2.0 streams individual applications.

questions.prompt: A software vendor wants to stream a desktop application to users' browsers without delivering full desktops. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: AppStream 2.0 streams applications to a browser; WorkSpaces provides full virtual desktops.

questions.prompt: A mobile team wants to test its app on many real phones and tablets hosted by AWS. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Device Farm lets you test apps on real mobile devices and browsers in the AWS Cloud.

questions.prompt: A Lambda function must run every day at midnight. Which service can invoke it on that schedule without servers?
questions.explanation: EventBridge Scheduler (or a scheduled EventBridge rule) can invoke targets such as Lambda on cron or rate schedules.

questions.prompt: Which open-source framework uses a simplified template syntax that extends CloudFormation to define serverless applications?
questions.explanation: AWS SAM provides shorthand syntax for functions, APIs and tables that transforms into CloudFormation.

questions.prompt: A partner needs to upload files to Amazon S3 using SFTP, as they do today with an on-premises server. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Transfer Family provides managed SFTP, FTPS and FTP endpoints backed by S3 or EFS.

questions.prompt: Which service provides managed Apache Airflow for orchestrating data pipelines?
choices: AWS Glue Data Catalog crawlers and jobs
Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow
questions.explanation: Amazon MWAA runs Apache Airflow without managing the underlying infrastructure.

questions.prompt: A company wants to run lightweight code at CloudFront edge locations to modify requests and responses close to viewers. Which feature fits?
questions.explanation: Lambda@Edge and CloudFront Functions run code at edge locations to customize content delivery.

questions.prompt: Analysts want to clean and normalize data visually, without writing code, before analysis. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: DataBrew is a visual data preparation tool with many prebuilt transformations.

questions.prompt: Traffic to an application rises sharply every Monday at 9 AM. Which EC2 Auto Scaling approach adds capacity just before this predictable spike?
questions.explanation: Scheduled scaling changes capacity at specific times for predictable load patterns.

questions.prompt: Which S3 storage class provides consistent single-digit millisecond access for the most latency-sensitive, frequently accessed data in a single Availability Zone?
questions.explanation: S3 Express One Zone is a high-performance single-AZ class for latency-sensitive workloads.

questions.prompt: Which Elastic Load Balancing type is designed to deploy, scale and manage third-party virtual appliances such as firewalls and intrusion detection systems?
questions.explanation: Gateway Load Balancer distributes traffic to fleets of virtual appliances; ALB and NLB route to application targets.

questions.prompt: A company wants a fully managed, AWS-native container orchestration service and has no need for Kubernetes compatibility. Which service is MOST appropriate?
questions.explanation: Amazon ECS is AWS's own fully managed container orchestrator and can run tasks on EC2 or Fargate. EKS is the choice when Kubernetes compatibility is required.

questions.prompt: An EC2 Auto Scaling group should automatically keep average CPU utilization close to 50% as load rises and falls. Which scaling approach is BEST?
choices: Setting minimum and maximum capacity to the same value
questions.explanation: Target tracking adjusts capacity automatically to hold a metric such as average CPU at the chosen target value. Scheduled scaling only suits predictable, time-based changes.

questions.prompt: An Application Load Balancer finds that one registered EC2 instance is failing its health checks. What does Elastic Load Balancing do?
choices: Terminates the unhealthy instance and immediately launches a replacement in another AZ
Reboots the instance on new hardware
Stops routing requests to that instance until it passes health checks again
Opens a support case with AWS automatically
questions.explanation: The load balancer simply stops sending traffic to unhealthy targets and resumes when they are healthy. Replacing unhealthy instances is done by EC2 Auto Scaling, not the load balancer.

questions.prompt: What makes a subnet in an Amazon VPC a public subnet?
choices: It contains a NAT gateway for outbound traffic
It is created in an Availability Zone marked as public
Its network ACL allows all inbound traffic
Its route table has a route to an internet gateway
questions.explanation: A subnet is public when its associated route table sends internet-bound traffic (0.0.0.0/0) to an internet gateway. A NAT gateway gives private subnets outbound access only.

questions.prompt: A company wants to stop using physical tape libraries for backups while keeping its existing tape-based backup software. Which option fits BEST?
questions.explanation: Tape Gateway presents a virtual tape library to existing backup applications and stores the virtual tapes in Amazon S3 and S3 Glacier storage classes.

questions.prompt: A company runs NetApp ONTAP storage on premises and wants a fully managed AWS service with the same data management features, accessible over NFS, SMB and iSCSI. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP provides fully managed ONTAP file systems with multi-protocol access and familiar features such as snapshots and replication.

questions.prompt: A developer accidentally deleted important rows from an Amazon RDS database 20 minutes ago. Automated backups are enabled. What is the BEST way to recover the data?
choices: Force a failover to the Multi-AZ standby instance in the other Availability Zone
Promote a read replica to become the primary
Do a point-in-time restore to a new DB instance from before the deletion
Restart the DB instance so that it rolls back the most recent transactions
questions.explanation: Automated backups allow point-in-time restore to any second within the retention period. Read replicas and the Multi-AZ standby already contain the deletion because changes are replicated.

questions.prompt: A global application needs a relational database with fast local reads in several Regions and fast recovery if a whole Region becomes unavailable. Which option fits BEST?
questions.explanation: Aurora Global Database replicates a relational database to secondary Regions with low latency for local reads and cross-Region disaster recovery. Multi-AZ protects only within one Region, and DynamoDB is not relational.

questions.prompt: Employees want a generative AI assistant that answers questions and summarizes content using the company's own data, such as wikis and document repositories, while respecting existing access permissions. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Amazon Q Business is a generative AI assistant that connects to enterprise data sources and honors user permissions. Amazon Q Developer focuses on software development tasks.

questions.prompt: A storage team wants organization-wide visibility into Amazon S3 usage and activity trends across all accounts, with recommendations to reduce cost. Which feature should it use?
choices: S3 Inventory reports for a single bucket
questions.explanation: S3 Storage Lens provides dashboards and metrics on storage usage and activity across accounts and Regions, with cost-optimization and data-protection recommendations.

questions.prompt: An administrator needs to find all resources with a missing 'CostCenter' tag across several Regions and add the tag to them in bulk. Which tool should they use?
choices: Tag Editor in AWS Resource Groups
questions.explanation: Tag Editor lets you search for resources across Regions and services and add, edit or remove tags on many resources at once.

questions.prompt: A team wants to interactively search and analyze its application log data in Amazon CloudWatch Logs using a purpose-built query language. Which feature should it use?
questions.explanation: CloudWatch Logs Insights runs interactive queries against log groups in CloudWatch Logs. CloudTrail Lake queries API activity events, not application logs.

questions.prompt: A company is migrating an Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Which tool helps convert the database schema and code objects to the new engine?
questions.explanation: For heterogeneous migrations, AWS SCT (or DMS Schema Conversion) converts schema and code objects; AWS DMS then migrates the data itself.

questions.prompt: Which Amazon EBS volume type is the current general purpose SSD that lets you provision IOPS and throughput independently of volume size?
questions.explanation: gp3 volumes include baseline performance and let you add IOPS and throughput separately from capacity. gp2 performance scales with volume size.

questions.prompt: Each new order event must be delivered to three independent processing systems that each consume messages at their own pace. Which design is BEST?
choices: Send the event to one SQS standard queue that all three systems poll
Store the event in an S3 bucket and have each system list the bucket hourly
Publish to an SNS topic with one SQS queue subscribed per system
Write the event to a single EC2 instance that forwards it by email
questions.explanation: SNS-to-SQS fan-out copies each message to every subscribed queue, so each system processes its own copy independently. With a single shared queue, each message is consumed by only one system.

questions.prompt: An EC2 instance occasionally fails system status checks because of problems with the underlying AWS hardware. Which automated action can an Amazon CloudWatch alarm take to address this?
choices: Convert the instance to a Spot Instance to obtain new capacity
Move the instance to another AWS Region
Increase the instance's EBS volume size
Recover the instance onto healthy underlying hardware
questions.explanation: CloudWatch alarm EC2 actions include stop, terminate, reboot and recover. Recovery moves the instance to new hardware while keeping its instance ID, private IP and attached EBS volumes.

questions.prompt: An application runs on a single EC2 instance and must become highly available and scale automatically with demand. Which design is BEST?
choices: An Auto Scaling group across multiple AZs behind an Application Load Balancer
A larger EC2 instance type with more CPU and memory
Two EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone, each with an Elastic IP address
A single EC2 instance with a daily EBS snapshot schedule
questions.explanation: Spreading an Auto Scaling group across AZs removes single points of failure and adds capacity as needed, while the load balancer distributes traffic to healthy instances. A bigger instance is still a single point of failure.

questions.prompt: An administrator applied an S3 bucket policy that accidentally denies all principals, including the account's administrators. Who can remove this policy?
choices: Any user in the IAM Identity Center administrators group
Any IAM user with the AdministratorAccess policy
The AWS Support team on request
questions.explanation: Editing or deleting a bucket policy that denies all principals is one of the tasks that requires root user credentials, because the policy also blocks IAM administrators.

questions.prompt: A security review finds that access keys exist for the AWS account root user. What does AWS recommend?
choices: Store the root user access keys in AWS Secrets Manager
Rotate the root user access keys every 90 days
Delete the root access keys and use IAM roles for programmatic access
Keep the keys but require MFA for every API call made with the root access keys
questions.explanation: AWS recommends not having root user access keys at all, because they grant unrestricted access to the account. Permissions boundaries cannot be applied to the root user.

questions.prompt: Signed-in users of a mobile app need temporary AWS credentials so the app can upload their photos directly to an Amazon S3 bucket. Which feature provides these credentials?
choices: A separate IAM user for each app customer
Long-term IAM access keys built into the app
questions.explanation: Cognito identity pools exchange an authenticated identity for temporary, limited-privilege AWS credentials. Embedding long-term keys or creating IAM users per customer is insecure and does not scale.

questions.prompt: In AWS Control Tower, which type of control finds noncompliant resources after they are created, typically by using AWS Config rules?
questions.explanation: Detective controls detect and report noncompliance using AWS Config rules. Preventive controls use SCPs to block actions, and proactive controls check resources before they are provisioned.

questions.prompt: Why does AWS recommend running production and development workloads in separate AWS accounts?
choices: Separate accounts are required to use more than one AWS Region
Accounts are strong security and billing boundaries that limit the impact of mistakes
Each AWS account is placed on its own dedicated physical hardware in AWS data centers
Separate accounts remove the need for IAM policies
questions.explanation: An AWS account is a hard isolation boundary for resources, permissions and billing, so problems in one environment do not easily affect another. A multi-account structure is a core AWS best practice.

questions.prompt: A company must ensure that its backups cannot be deleted by anyone, including administrators, before their retention period ends. Which feature meets this requirement?
choices: An IAM permissions boundary on the backup administrator
AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode
questions.explanation: Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode enforces write-once-read-many protection so recovery points cannot be deleted or have retention shortened, even by the root user, once the lock is in effect.

questions.prompt: A three-tier web application stores customer data in an Amazon RDS database. Where should the database be placed for the BEST security?
choices: In a public subnet with a network ACL that allows all traffic
In a public subnet with a public IP address and a strong master password
In the same public subnet as the web servers
In private subnets, accepting traffic only from the application tier
questions.explanation: Placing databases in private subnets with no route from the internet, and allowing access only from the application tier, reduces the attack surface. A strong password alone does not prevent exposure.

questions.prompt: A database's security group must allow connections only from the application servers, whose IP addresses change as Auto Scaling replaces them. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Use the application tier's security group as the source in the inbound rule
Add each application server's current private IP address as a separate rule
Allow inbound traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 on the database port
Use a network ACL to allow the whole VPC CIDR range
questions.explanation: A security group rule can reference another security group, so any instance in the application tier is allowed automatically regardless of its IP address. Opening to 0.0.0.0/0 would expose the database.

questions.prompt: On-premises servers need to call AWS APIs without storing long-term access keys. Which feature lets them obtain temporary credentials by using X.509 certificates?
questions.explanation: IAM Roles Anywhere lets workloads outside AWS use X.509 certificates from a trusted certificate authority to assume IAM roles and receive temporary credentials.

questions.prompt: A small team wants its public web application protected against common exploits such as those in the OWASP Top 10 without writing and maintaining its own rules. What should it use?
choices: Security groups on the web servers
AWS Managed Rules rule groups in AWS WAF
questions.explanation: AWS Managed Rules are prebuilt WAF rule groups, maintained by AWS, that protect against common web exploits. Shield Standard protects against DDoS attacks, and security groups cannot inspect HTTP content.

questions.prompt: A team moves its self-managed MySQL server to Amazon RDS. Which task does the team still own?
choices: Maintaining the physical network in the data center
Patching the operating system of the underlying database host
Managing database users and security group access rules
questions.explanation: With RDS, AWS manages the underlying infrastructure and host OS, while the customer controls database users, security groups and other access settings.

questions.prompt: Which policy is the primary way to control who can use and manage an AWS KMS key?
choices: The key policy attached to the KMS key
A tag policy in AWS Organizations
questions.explanation: Every KMS key has a key policy, which is the primary resource-based policy controlling access to it. IAM policies only take effect when the key policy allows them.

questions.prompt: A company wants every new Amazon EBS volume created in a Region to be encrypted automatically, without relying on each user to choose encryption. What should it enable?
choices: EBS encryption by default for the account in that Region
S3 Block Public Access at the account level for all buckets
AWS Shield Advanced for the account
questions.explanation: Turning on EBS encryption by default makes the account encrypt all new EBS volumes and snapshot copies in that Region with a KMS key.

questions.prompt: A company wants to make sure that nobody in the accounts of an organizational unit can stop or delete AWS CloudTrail trails, including account administrators. What is the MOST effective control?
choices: An Amazon CloudWatch dashboard that displays the status of each trail
A cost allocation tag on each trail
An SCP that denies the CloudTrail StopLogging and DeleteTrail actions
An IAM password policy in each account
questions.explanation: SCPs set guardrails that apply to all IAM users and roles in member accounts, including administrators, so a deny on cloudtrail:StopLogging and cloudtrail:DeleteTrail cannot be overridden there.

questions.prompt: A CloudTrail trail is not showing Amazon S3 object-level activity such as GetObject and PutObject calls. What must be configured to capture these events?
choices: VPC Flow Logs for the VPC
Logging of data events for the S3 buckets
questions.explanation: Trails log management events by default, but data events such as S3 object-level operations must be enabled explicitly and incur additional charges.

questions.prompt: A team monitors key business metrics and configures automation so that when a threshold is breached the workload recovers on its own. Which Reliability design principle is this?
questions.explanation: The Reliability pillar's 'automatically recover from failure' principle uses monitoring of KPIs to trigger automated recovery. Testing recovery procedures is about validating recovery, not performing it automatically.

questions.prompt: A team chooses a key-value database for simple lookups and a graph database for relationship queries, matching each technology to how the data is actually used. Which Performance Efficiency design principle does this reflect?
questions.explanation: Mechanical sympathy means using the technology approach that aligns best with your goals and data access patterns. Adopting a consumption model is a Cost Optimization principle.

questions.prompt: A security team regularly runs incident response simulations and uses tools to speed up detection, investigation and recovery. Which Security pillar design principle is this?
choices: Protect data in transit and at rest
questions.explanation: Preparing for security events includes having incident management processes and running simulations so the team can respond quickly when something happens.

questions.prompt: A company moves workloads to newer, more efficient instance types mainly to reduce the energy needed to do the same work. Which Well-Architected pillar is it primarily applying?
questions.explanation: The Sustainability pillar includes the principle 'anticipate and adopt new, more efficient hardware and software offerings' to reduce environmental impact.

questions.prompt: Before launching a new feature, a team runs exercises to identify potential sources of failure and tests how the workload behaves when those failures happen. Which Operational Excellence design principle is this?
questions.explanation: 'Anticipate failure' means performing pre-mortem exercises and testing failure scenarios so their impact is understood and removed or mitigated before they occur.

questions.prompt: Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework perspective includes cloud financial management, alongside capabilities such as program management and risk management?
questions.explanation: The Governance perspective covers capabilities such as program and project management, benefits management, risk management and cloud financial management.

questions.prompt: In which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework phase does an organization identify and prioritize transformation opportunities in line with its strategic objectives?
questions.explanation: The Envision phase demonstrates how the cloud can accelerate business outcomes by identifying and prioritizing transformation opportunities. Align then identifies capability gaps.

questions.prompt: Which term describes a system's ability to continue operating without interruption even when some of its components fail?
questions.explanation: Fault tolerance means the system keeps working through component failures, usually through redundancy. Durability refers to data not being lost, and elasticity to matching capacity to demand.

questions.prompt: An application is broken into small, independently deployable services that each own a business capability and communicate through well-defined APIs. What is this architectural style called?
questions.explanation: A microservices architecture splits an application into independent services that can be developed, deployed and scaled separately, unlike a monolith where all parts are deployed together.

questions.prompt: Which statement BEST describes serverless computing on AWS?
choices: AWS removes the need to write any application code
AWS manages the servers; it scales automatically and you pay for what you use
You rent dedicated physical servers by the month
Applications run on no physical hardware at all, only on virtual network functions
questions.explanation: Serverless services such as AWS Lambda still run on servers, but AWS manages them; customers get automatic scaling, built-in availability and pay-for-use pricing.

questions.prompt: A web application stores user session data in Amazon ElastiCache instead of in memory on each web server. Which benefit does this MOST directly enable?
choices: Session data no longer needs to be encrypted
The application must now run in a single Availability Zone to keep sessions consistent
Stateless web servers that can be added or removed freely to scale horizontally
The web servers no longer need a load balancer
questions.explanation: Moving session state out of the servers makes the web tier stateless, so any instance can serve any request and the tier can scale out and in without losing sessions.

questions.prompt: A team regularly simulates events such as Availability Zone failures in production to practice its response and improve the workload. Which general Well-Architected design principle does this follow?
choices: Automate to make architectural experimentation easier
questions.explanation: The general design principle 'improve through game days' recommends regularly scheduled simulations of production events to find areas for improvement and build experience handling them.

questions.prompt: Which AWS Trusted Advisor category includes the check that flags Amazon RDS DB instances not configured for Multi-AZ deployment?
questions.explanation: Fault tolerance checks look for ways to increase availability and redundancy, such as RDS Multi-AZ, EBS snapshots and instances spread across AZs.

questions.prompt: A new application's Amazon DynamoDB table will have unpredictable traffic that varies widely from hour to hour. Which capacity mode is the simplest and MOST cost-effective starting point?
choices: Provisioned capacity set to the minimum allowed
Provisioned capacity set for the expected peak
Provisioned capacity with reserved capacity purchased
questions.explanation: On-demand mode charges per request and scales instantly, so you do not pay for unused provisioned throughput when traffic is unpredictable. Provisioning for the peak wastes money most of the time.

questions.prompt: An organization uses consolidated billing in AWS Organizations. Which account is responsible for paying the charges of all member accounts?
choices: Each member account pays its own bill separately
The account with the highest monthly spend
questions.explanation: With consolidated billing, the management account receives one combined bill and pays the charges incurred by all member accounts.

questions.prompt: A developer wants an application to programmatically retrieve current AWS service prices to build an internal cost tool. Which option should they use?
questions.explanation: The AWS Price List API returns current prices for AWS services in a machine-readable format. The Pricing Calculator is an interactive web tool, and the CUR shows your own past usage.

questions.prompt: A finance team wants to group AWS costs into custom categories such as 'Marketing' and 'Research', using rules based on accounts, tags and services, and see them in billing tools. Which feature fits?
questions.explanation: AWS Cost Categories let you define rules that map costs to your own business structure; the categories then appear in Cost Explorer, Budgets and the Cost and Usage Report.

questions.prompt: Which Reserved Instance scope provides a capacity reservation for the instances in addition to a billing discount?
questions.explanation: Zonal Reserved Instances reserve capacity in the specified AZ. Regional RIs and Savings Plans give discounts and flexibility but do not reserve capacity.

questions.prompt: During its cloud transformation, a company expands its successful pilot initiatives into production across the wider business at the desired scale. Which AWS CAF phase is this?
questions.explanation: The AWS CAF phases are Envision, Align, Launch and Scale. Scale expands pilots in production to the desired scale; Launch is where the pilots are first delivered.

questions.prompt: Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework perspective includes capabilities such as strategy management, data monetization and business insights?
questions.explanation: The Business perspective covers capabilities such as strategy management, portfolio management, data monetization and business insights.

questions.prompt: Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework perspective includes capabilities such as continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) and provisioning and orchestration?
questions.explanation: The Platform perspective covers platform engineering, provisioning and orchestration, modern application development and CI/CD.

questions.prompt: A company replaces long-term IAM user access keys with centrally managed identities, temporary credentials and least-privilege permissions. Which Security pillar design principle is it applying?
choices: Protect data in transit and at rest
questions.explanation: A strong identity foundation means least privilege, separation of duties, centralized identity management and avoiding long-term static credentials.

questions.prompt: A security team defines its security controls as code in version-controlled templates so they are deployed consistently and automatically. Which Security pillar design principle does this follow?
questions.explanation: Automating security best practices includes defining and managing security controls as code that is version controlled and deployed automatically.

questions.prompt: A team makes all infrastructure changes through automated, tested pipelines instead of manual console changes, so every change can be tracked and reviewed. Which Reliability design principle is this?
choices: Scale horizontally to increase aggregate workload availability
questions.explanation: The Reliability pillar recommends making infrastructure changes through automation so they can be tracked and reviewed, rather than by hand.

questions.prompt: A team instruments its workload to collect metrics, logs and traces tied to business outcomes so it can understand behaviour and act quickly on issues. Which Operational Excellence design principle is this?
questions.explanation: Implementing observability gives a full understanding of workload behaviour, performance and business outcomes so teams can make informed decisions and respond to issues.

questions.prompt: A company creates a dedicated function that brings finance and technology teams together to build cost awareness and own cloud spending processes. Which Cost Optimization design principle is this?
questions.explanation: Implementing Cloud Financial Management means investing in the people, processes and partnerships that build cost awareness across the organization.

questions.prompt: A company consolidates several lightly loaded EC2 instances onto fewer instances that run at higher utilization, mainly to reduce the energy its workload consumes. Which Sustainability design principle is this?
choices: Anticipate and adopt new, more efficient hardware and software offerings
Reduce the downstream impact of your cloud workloads
questions.explanation: Maximizing utilization means right-sizing and consolidating so fewer, busier resources do the work, because idle capacity still consumes energy.

questions.prompt: A company optimizes its mobile app to send less data and run well on older devices, so customers do not need to upgrade their phones. Which Sustainability design principle does this reflect?
choices: Anticipate and adopt new, more efficient hardware and software offerings
Reduce the downstream impact of your cloud workloads
questions.explanation: This principle reduces the energy and resources customers need to use your service, including reducing the need for them to upgrade their devices.

questions.prompt: A team moves a workload to AWS Lambda and Amazon DynamoDB so it no longer runs and maintains servers for traditional compute activities. Which Performance Efficiency design principle is this?
questions.explanation: Serverless architectures remove the need to run and maintain physical servers, and AWS manages the underlying infrastructure.

questions.prompt: Which general Well-Architected design principle recognises that automation and on-demand testing in the cloud make it lower risk to change a workload's design as requirements change over time?
questions.explanation: In the cloud, automation and on-demand testing lower the risk of design changes, so architectures can evolve instead of being fixed at the start.

questions.prompt: A team collects data on how its architecture choices affect workload behaviour and uses that data to make fact-based design decisions. Which general Well-Architected design principle is this?
choices: Automate with architectural experimentation in mind
questions.explanation: Driving architectures using data means collecting data on how choices affect the workload and using it to make fact-based improvements.

questions.prompt: Foundations, workload architecture, change management and failure management are best practice areas of which Well-Architected pillar?
questions.explanation: These four areas make up the Reliability pillar, which focuses on a workload performing its intended function correctly and consistently.

questions.prompt: Detection, infrastructure protection, data protection and incident response are best practice areas of which Well-Architected pillar?
questions.explanation: These are best practice areas of the Security pillar, alongside identity and access management, security foundations and application security.

questions.prompt: Expenditure and usage awareness, cost-effective resources, and managing demand and supplying resources are best practice areas of which Well-Architected pillar?
questions.explanation: These are best practice areas of the Cost Optimization pillar, together with practicing Cloud Financial Management and optimizing over time.

questions.prompt: A company uses AWS CloudFormation templates to create identical test environments on demand and delete them when testing ends. Which cloud economics benefit does this automation MOST directly provide?
choices: No charges for any resources that are created by templates
Reserved Instance discounts applied automatically to each new stack
Lower hourly prices for the EC2 instances that the templates launch
Less manual work and fewer errors, paying only while resources exist
questions.explanation: Automation cuts labour and configuration errors, and tearing environments down stops charges. CloudFormation does not change resource prices; you pay for what it creates.

questions.prompt: Under the shared responsibility model for sustainability, what is AWS responsible for?
choices: Choosing efficient instance types and Regions for each customer workload
Efficient data centers, including their power, cooling and hardware
Deleting unused data that customers keep in their S3 buckets
Rightsizing customer workloads so they match actual demand
questions.explanation: AWS is responsible for sustainability of the cloud, meaning efficient global infrastructure. Customers are responsible for sustainability in the cloud, such as rightsizing and data management.

questions.prompt: In the AWS Migration Acceleration Program, which phase focuses on creating a detailed migration plan, building a secure landing zone and closing readiness gaps found earlier?
questions.explanation: The MAP phases are Assess, Mobilize, and Migrate and Modernize. Mobilize builds the detailed plan, landing zone and operating model, and closes gaps found during Assess.

questions.prompt: Which term describes the percentage of time that a workload is operational and able to serve requests?
questions.explanation: Availability is the share of time a workload is usable. Durability is about data not being lost over time.

questions.prompt: A web application and its database both run on a single EC2 instance in one Availability Zone. Which risk does this design MOST clearly present?
choices: Higher data transfer charges between the web tier and the database
A single point of failure that can take the whole application offline
No ability to use security groups to restrict network access
Automatic loss of all stored data whenever the instance stops
questions.explanation: With everything on one instance in one AZ, a single instance or AZ failure stops the whole application. Data on EBS volumes is not lost just because an instance stops.

questions.prompt: A company aligns each operations team to a specific business outcome so that teams understand how their work contributes to that result. Which Operational Excellence design principle is this?
choices: Learn from all operational events and metrics
questions.explanation: Organizing teams around business outcomes is an Operational Excellence design principle, with leadership vision and team ownership aligned to business results.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF)?
choices: To estimate the monthly cost of a proposed AWS architecture
To certify that customer workloads meet compliance standards
To review individual workloads against AWS architectural best practices
To help organizations plan and speed up their cloud transformation
questions.explanation: AWS CAF draws on AWS experience to help organizations identify and prioritize transformation opportunities. Reviewing individual workloads is the role of the Well-Architected Framework.

questions.prompt: In the AWS Well-Architected Framework, what does the term 'workload' mean?
choices: A set of components that together deliver business value
A monthly report that shows usage for each AWS service
A single AWS account together with all of the resources inside it
The CPU and memory load measured on a single EC2 instance
